full_text_en:
China Ship Fuel Supply Company Tianjin Branch v. Hong Kong Dashun Shipping Co., Ltd. — dispute over compensation for ship collision damage

Plaintiff: China Ship Fuel Supply Company Tianjin Branch.

Legal Representative: Zhang Ruifu, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Wei Lixian, Deputy Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Tongnian, Lawyer of Tianjin Economic-Technological Development Zone Law Office.

Defendant: Hong Kong Dashun Shipping Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Chen Wubo, General Manager of the Company.

Agents ad litem: Ye Weiying and Gao Yifeng, Lawyers of China Global Law Office.

The Plaintiff, China Ship Fuel Supply Company Tianjin Branch, filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin Maritime Court against Hong Kong Dashun Shipping Co., Ltd. regarding a dispute over compensation for ship collision damage. The Tianjin Maritime Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and, after public trial, found the following facts:

At 20:22 on February 8, 1987, there was a southeast wind of force 2 in the anchorage of Dalian Port, with fog. The fog spread from southeast to northwest, gradually increasing in density. At approximately 20:45 on the same day, the vessel "Jinyou No. 6" (length 94.4 meters, breadth 14.2 meters, depth 7.1 meters, main engine diesel 3200 hp) owned by China Ship Fuel Supply Company Tianjin Branch (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin Branch), fully loaded with 4,000 tons of light diesel oil, departed from the Ganjingzi berth in Dalian and returned to Tianjin Xingang. Both radars of the vessel were functioning normally, visual range was about 1-2 nautical miles, and the vessel entered the channel on a compass course of 90° at a speed of about 10 knots. At approximately 20:52, it was abeam to port of Dalian Port No. 6 light buoy. At approximately 21:04, it was abeam to port of No. 4 light buoy. After sailing for another 8 minutes, "Jinyou No. 6" changed course to compass course 180°, sailing from north to south across the No. 1 cargo vessel quarantine anchorage, with visibility reduced to only 100-200 meters. Under these circumstances, "Jinyou No. 6" did not post a lookout, did not use radar for continuous observation, and continued sailing at a speed of about 10 knots. At this time, "Jinyou No. 6" visually detected the vessel "Ruby" operated by Hong Kong Dashun Shipping Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Dashun Shipping) approximately 200 meters ahead, and immediately took action with hard-a-starboard rudder and stopping engines. However, due to the close distance between the two vessels, in less than one minute, the starboard bow section of "Jinyou No. 6" collided with the port side of the first hold of "Ruby". After the incident, mediation by the local competent authority failed, and Tianjin Branch filed a lawsuit with the court, alleging that "Ruby" was anchored in an improper position, was negligent in radar lookout in fog, failed to keep a proper lookout, and did not sound fog signals as required. Tianjin Branch requested that Dashun Shipping bear, in proportion to its liability, the repair costs of both vessels, survey fees, and operating losses and tank cleaning costs of "Jinyou No. 6", totaling RMB 1,729,444.10.

The vessel "Ruby" (overall length 146.44 meters, breadth 22.6 meters, depth 12 meters, gross tonnage 12,087 tons) operated by Dashun Shipping was anchored at the No. 1 cargo vessel quarantine anchorage of Dalian Port at the time of the incident, with an anchor position bearing true 193° from Huangbaizui Lighthouse, distance 1.5 nautical miles. From 20:00 to 24:00 on that day, the vessel's watch personnel observed fog forming on the sea surface, with visibility of 100 meters. Although the deck log of "Ruby" recorded that actions were taken according to the rules, it did not specify the specific actions. The captain stated that at 21:08, the third officer sounded one fog signal (one prolonged blast). However, the third officer stated that at 21:05, following the captain's order, he immediately sounded the whistle, one prolonged and one short blast. In the statement of defense, it was further stated: "In the fog, the gong was struck, but there was no time to ring the bell." Clearly, the fog signals were not sounded as required. Dashun Shipping argued in its defense that the anchor position of "Ruby" did not exceed the prescribed anchorage range; the radar was switched on when fog set in; there was no negligence in lookout; and that although the bell was not rung while anchored in fog, this was not the cause of the collision. Dashun Shipping also counterclaimed that "Jinyou No. 6" violated regulations by crossing the anchorage, sailing at high speed in fog, failing to use radar properly, neglecting lookout, failing to sound fog signals, and taking improper collision avoidance measures, thereby causing the collision, and that the company should bear full collision liability. It requested that Tianjin Branch bear the operating losses and additional fuel costs of "Ruby", totaling USD 117,075.66.

The Tianjin Maritime Court held that "Jinyou No. 6" was a power-driven vessel underway. When departing the port, it did not follow the course prescribed by the "Dalian Port Dashan Waterway Traffic Separation Scheme"; it turned prematurely at a distance of 2 nautical miles from light buoy H2, crossing the anchorage from north to south, which constituted a serious violation of navigation rules. While navigating under conditions of extremely poor visibility, it neither posted a lookout nor used radar for continuous observation, relying solely on visual navigation. After entering the fog area, it sailed at excessive speed in an environment with relatively high vessel traffic density, and also failed to sound fog bell signals. The above circumstances were the primary causes of the collision. In summary, "Jinyou No. 6" violated Article 14 of the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and Rules 5, 6, 7(2), 19(2), and 35(1) of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972, and shall bear primary liability for the ship collision.

At the time of the collision, "Ruby" was anchored in fog, and its anchor position did not exceed the prescribed anchorage range. However, while anchored under conditions of poor visibility, it failed to sound fog signals as required, thereby preventing "Jinyou No. 6" from receiving early warning of collision danger. "Ruby" was negligent in the performance of its duties, violating Rule 35(6) of the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972, and shall also bear certain liability for the collision.

With respect to the compensation items and amounts claimed by the Plaintiff and the Defendant, in accordance with Article 117, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China concerning "Anyone who damages state property or the property of a collective or another person shall restore the property to its original condition or reimburse the expense incurred" and "If the victim suffers other major losses as a result, the infringer shall also compensate for those losses", the People's Bank of China's "Provisions on Interest Calculation Methods and Loan Interest Rates", and with reference to international shipping practices, after verification and calculation, it was determined that the economic losses and interest of Tianjin Branch amounted to USD 387,588.30; and the economic losses and interest of Dashun Shipping amounted to USD 66,318.51.

On the basis of ascertaining the facts and distinguishing liability, the Tianjin Maritime Court, in accordance with Article 97 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), presided over mediation, and the parties reached the following agreement on April 29, 1988:

The Plaintiff, China Ship Fuel Supply Company Tianjin Branch, agreed to bear 90% of the liability for this maritime casualty, i.e., to bear the economic losses of both parties amounting to USD 408,516.13; Hong Kong Dashun Shipping Co., Ltd. agreed to bear 10% of the liability, i.e., to bear the economic losses of both parties amounting to USD 45,390.68.
